questions.q: What is the key difference between Continuous Delivery and Continuous Deployment?
options: Continuous Delivery only applies to sandboxes, Continuous Deployment only applies to production
Continuous Delivery automatically prepares a release but a human approves the final push; Continuous Deployment removes that human approval gate entirely
There is no difference, the terms are interchangeable
Continuous Deployment only runs unit tests, while Continuous Delivery runs no tests at all
questions.explain: Continuous Delivery stops just short of releasing automatically, leaving a human to approve the final step; Continuous Deployment ships automatically to anything that passes every check.

questions.q: Why is a Salesforce deployment fundamentally different from deploying a typical web app to a server?
options: Salesforce deployments never involve any automated testing
Salesforce has no concept of an org at all
Web app deployments and Salesforce deployments are identical in every respect
A Salesforce deployment moves metadata into an already-running, live org rather than shipping a compiled binary or container to a provisioned server
questions.explain: There's no binary artifact in a Salesforce deployment — metadata is sent to a live, already-running org, which is why validating changes before they land matters so much.

questions.q: What does a project's sfdx-project.json file declare?
options: The project's package directories and related DX settings
The org's Apex test coverage percentage
The GitHub Actions workflow triggers
The list of Salesforce users with CI access
questions.explain: sfdx-project.json is the DX project manifest; it declares packageDirectories and other project-level settings the CLI reads.

questions.q: Why do modern Salesforce CI/CD pipelines work against DX source format rather than raw metadata API format or Change Sets?
options: Metadata API format cannot be deployed by any CLI tool
Source format removes the need for any Apex tests
Source format is organized the way a developer actually works and produces a readable Git diff, which is what makes pull requests and automated pipeline steps possible
Change Sets are actually the standard tool used in every CI/CD pipeline
questions.explain: Source format's per-object, per-component layout is designed to be readable in a Git diff — the foundation every later pipeline step (PR review, automated validation, automated deploy) depends on.

questions.q: This course assumes you already know which prior skill set?
options: Working inside Salesforce Setup as an administrator, from the Salesforce Administrator path
Writing production Java microservices
Kubernetes cluster administration
No prior Salesforce knowledge is assumed at all
questions.explain: This course builds on the completed Salesforce Administrator path and does not re-teach Setup, Flow, or the object model — it focuses on what changes once a team automates delivery of changes to those same orgs.
